subject: Site integration: node-farm sizing + customer local storage handoff
messages:
From: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@groundsite.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: ops@groundsite.com
Date: 2028-03-08T09:12:00Z
Subject: On-prem cluster handoff and local storage constraints

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for walking our infra team through the architecture yesterday. We finished an on-site inventory this morning and attached a quick CSV with disk mappings and SAN/LVM allocations. A couple of constraints to flag: the on-site backup LUNs are on an older controller and we were advised to minimize steady-state IO to them. Also, the site runs a small cross-connect VLAN pool that should not be overloaded.

We need Redwood's recommended node sizing and a short list of required kernel/OS settings so our infra folks can apply them before the hardware handoff next week. Can you confirm the expected PV class behavior for local NVMe disks vs. attached SAN? Also, who on your side will own live cutover runbook ops on day-of?

Thanks,
Tom
Ops Lead, GroundSite Health
attachments: site-inventory.csv (text/csv)

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
To: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@groundsite.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: 2028-03-08T12:03:00Z
Subject: Re: On-prem cluster handoff and local storage constraints

Tom — thanks for the inventory. I pulled a quick pass and added three immediate notes below. I attached a node-farm sizing workbook with two capacity scenarios (baseline / burst-ready) and a network port diagram callout for the compute leafs.

Top-level recommendations:
- Use NVMe-backed nodes for GPU workloads (local-ssd PV class) and prefer ReadMostly mount options where possible to avoid controller write amplification.
- Configure a distinct StorageClass for SAN-backed blockstore (claim: san-block) with reclaimPolicy: Retain and explicit nodeAffinity to storage gateway hosts.
- Limit cross-connect usage: reserve two spare VLANs on the same switch to handle DR and kube-proxy healthcheck traffic.

OS/Kernal/Kube settings to apply before handoff (short list):
- disable transparent_hugepage and set vm.swappiness=10
- set net.core.somaxconn=1024 and tcp_tw_reuse=1
- kubelet: --eviction-hard=imagefs.available<5%,nodefs.available<5% and set eviction-minimum-reclaim to cpu=100m,memory=200Mi

Handoff ownership: Marissa will lead the day-of runbook and Irena will be the on-call engineering responder. I will coordinate the canary rollout plan and preflight tests.

Next steps: please confirm which VLAN IDs we can consume and whether the site team can map the NVMe devices to stable device-ids (we prefer stable dev-ids or udev rules instead of relying on ephemeral names).

—Stephanie
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachments: node-farm-sizing.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet), network-ports-diagram.pdf (application/pdf)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@groundsite.com>, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: 2028-03-09T08:20:00Z
Subject: Re: On-prem cluster handoff and local storage constraints

Tom — quick technical clarifications from the infra playbook side:
- For local NVMe PVs we recommend using device-plugin + local-static-provisioner with an explicit topology key of topology.kubernetes.io/zone set to the node-rack id. That keeps scheduling tight and avoids cross-rack IO.
- SAN-backed volumes should be treated as long-lived backing stores (encrypted at rest via host KMS). We will not assume volume detachment speed for critical pods; prefer read-only or replicated caches for latency-sensitive workloads.
- If the backup controller cannot handle sustained writes, add a write-through cache (btrfs or dm-cache) on gateway hosts; we can provide a small RPM to bootstrap that.

I produced a short preflight checklist in the sizing workbook (tab: preflight) — please run the NVMe burn-in tests and paste the results into the sheet. We will gate the canary until burn-in passes.

Marissa
Technical Delivery, Redwood Inference
attachment: none

From: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@groundsite.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: 2028-03-10T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: On-prem cluster handoff and local storage constraints

Thanks all — confirming VLANs 142 and 143 are reserved for Redwood, NVMe device mapping will be set via udev rules (we'll send the rules file by EOD), and the SAN team will provision a read-only mirror LUN for canary reads. We'll run the NVMe burn-in tonight and update the workbook with results tomorrow morning.

Tom
Ops Lead, GroundSite Health
attachments: udev-mapping.rules (text/plain)
